Loading required packages

```{r}
# Loading packages
pacman::p_load(rvest, tidyverse, xml2, ipumsr, janitor)
```

## Section 1

### Part 1: Authentication

I followed the steps in the assignment to create my account, generate an API key, and set it in my environment. Those steps are not included here for security, but I used the `set_ipums_api_key()` function to do this.

### Part 2: The Data Challenge

In this section, I used the commands listed in the assignment instructions to 1) Define, 2) Submit, 3) Wait & Download, and 4) Read the required file (1990 State Population Status for all states). I had to go to the [IPUMS website](https://tech.popdata.org/ipumsr/articles/ipums.html) to get help with the commands.

Note: I also set this chunk of code to `eval: false` so that the request does not download the data again.

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Part 2 - The Data Challenge
# Extract 1990 State Populations Status (Table NP1) for all states
# First, define the request
nhgis_request <- define_extract_agg(
  collection = "nhgis",
  description = "NHGIS Data via IPUMS API",
  datasets = ds_spec(
    "1990_STF1",
    data_tables = "NP1",
    geog_levels = "state"
  )
)
# Second, submit the request
submit_extract(nhgis_request, api_key = Sys.getenv("IPUMS_API_KEY"))

# Wait 
nhgis_request <- wait_for_extract(
  "nhgis:1",
  initial_delay_seconds = 0,
  max_delay_seconds = 300,
  timeout_seconds = 10800,
  verbose = TRUE,
  api_key = Sys.getenv("IPUMS_API_KEY")
)

# Download
downloaded_files <- download_extract(
  nhgis_request,
  download_dir = getwd(),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE,
  api_key = Sys.getenv("IPUMS_API_KEY")
)
```

The file is read and examined afterward with the following code:

```{r}
# Read the File
data_file <- "nhgis0001_csv.zip"
nhgis_data <- read_ipums_agg(data_file)

#look at file metadata
ipums_var_info(nhgis_data)
```

### Part 3: Data Cleaning

As requested, I selected and renamed the columns of the dataframe with the following code:

```{r}
#Part 3 - Data Cleaning
#select and rename columns

nhgis_clean <- nhgis_data |> 
  select(
    gisjoin = GISJOIN,
    year = YEAR,
    state_abbr = STUSAB,
    division = DIVISIONA,
    region = REGIONA,
    state_name = STATE,
    state_code = STATEA,
    land_area = AREALAND,
    water_area = AREAWAT,
    total_pop = ET1001
  )

#Check to make sure it worked
head(nhgis_clean) 
```

### Part 4: Find the population density

In order to do this, I had to first convert the `land_area` vector to a numeric class, as it was originally a character class. Then, I used the equation provided, (population density = total population / land area), to calculate the population density of each state. I used the `mutate()` function to do both.

```{r}
#Part 4 Find Population Density
head(nhgis_clean) #check column types

nhgis_clean <- nhgis_clean |> 
  mutate(
    land_area = parse_number(land_area), #need to convert this to numeric from chr
    pop_density = total_pop / land_area #calculate the new column
  )

head(nhgis_clean) #check to make sure it worked
```

### Part 5: Find Water Share

Similar to above, I needed to convert the `water_area` vector to a numeric class and calculate the water share with the given equation: water share = water area /(land area + water area). Once again, I used the `mutate()` function for both steps.

```{r}
#Part 5 calculate Water Share

nhgis_clean <- nhgis_clean |> 
  mutate(
    water_area = parse_number(water_area), #convert water area to numeric
    water_share = water_area / (land_area + water_area) #calculate the new column
  )

head(nhgis_clean) #check work
```

## Section 2 - Scraping with Rvest

### Part 1 - Import the correct Table

I used the code included in one of our resource files, `WebscrapingTables.R` to first create a tibble of all of the tables on the website, then save the first one as the one that we want to work with.

```{r}
#Section 2 with the code from the Example File
wikiurl <- read_html(
  "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population"
)

#Creates a tibble of all of tables on the site
datatables <- wikiurl |>
  html_table()

#choose the first table and store it
ranking_table <- datatables[[1]]

#view it to confirm
ranking_table

```

### Part 2 - Clean the Column Names

I decided to manually rename the columns instead of using the `janitor` package because some names were blank, some had brackets (`[]`), and the extra text in the first data row had information with the year the values were from. Then, I deleted this first row of extra text as well as the last four rows which had summary data.

```{r}
#Part 2 - Clean the names & get rid of extra rows

#View the column names
names(ranking_table)

#rename them
names(ranking_table) <- c(
  "rank",
  "state",
  "population_estimate_2025",
  "population_2020",
  "house_seats",
  "house_seat_percent",
  "population_per_electoral_vote_2020",
  "population_per_house_seat_2020",
  "us_population_percent_2020",
  "electoral_college_percent_2020"
)

#get rid of the first row of extra text & the last 4 rows of summary data
clean_table <- ranking_table |>
  slice(2:(n() - 4))

#view the table
clean_table
```

### Part 3 - Set Column Class, Clean Up State Names, and include NAs

Finally, I corrected the column types with the `mutate()` function and `as.integer()`, `parse_number()` and used math functions to convert percentage values to decimals. I also noticed that there were some text in brackets in some of the territory names and used `str_remove()` to get rid of those.

This workflow forced `NA's` into the integer column, and also converted some of the `--` values in other columns to `NA` as well, which is what we wanted.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#Part 3 - Fix the column types & get rid of extra text in state column

clean_table2 <- clean_table |> mutate(
  rank = as.integer(rank),
  state = str_remove_all(state, "\\[[^]]*\\]"),
  population_estimate_2025 = parse_number(population_estimate_2025),
  population_2020 = parse_number(population_2020),
  house_seats = parse_number(house_seats),
  house_seat_percent = (parse_number(house_seat_percent)/100),
  population_per_electoral_vote_2020 = parse_number(population_per_electoral_vote_2020),
  population_per_house_seat_2020 = parse_number(population_per_house_seat_2020),
  us_population_percent_2020 = (parse_number(us_population_percent_2020)/100),
  electoral_college_percent_2020 = (parse_number(electoral_college_percent_2020)/100)
)

#check work
glimpse(clean_table2)
```
